native_result.query: The effect of which variable on BA degree completion decreases from 0.5024 to 0.0923 (while becoming insignifcant) when both SES and academic characteristics are included in analysis?
native_result.HypoA: The effect of SES on BA degree completion decreases from 0.3636  (significant) to  -0.2293 (insignificant) and effect of race on BA degree completion decreases from 0.5024  (significant) to 0.0923 (insignificant) when academic characteristics are considered.
native_result.HypoB: The effect of RACE (SAMPLE_RACE) — specifically the Black vs. White contrast — on BA degree completion decreases from a large, statistically significant unadjusted coefficient to ≈0.09 (log-odds, p≈0.68, insignificant) once both SES and the academic characteristics (ABILITY composite test score and PERCENTILE IN CLASS) are included. The Black–White racial gap in BA completion is therefore largely explained by (mediated through) differences in socioeconomic status and academic performance rather than by race itself.
native_result.WorkflowB: Loaded data/nls_ses_processed.csv (8773 rows, dropped redundant index column), verified no missing values and 2.7% BA-completion base rate. Computed candidate-vs-block correlations (FAMILY SIZE) and mean differences of SES/ABILITY/PERCENTILE across SAMPLE_RACE and SAMPLE_SEX categories. Fit logistic regression (statsmodels.Logit) for each demographic candidate: unadjusted (candidate only) and adjusted (candidate + SES + ABILITY + PERCENTILE IN CLASS), with White (race) and Female (sex) as reference categories, reporting coefficient, SE, and Wald p-value on both unstandardized and standardized scales. All models converged with no separation warnings. Matched the 0.0923/insignificant signature to the adjusted BLACK racial dummy (0.0926, p=0.6801).
